title: Investigate recurrent Taoyuan accident corridors before prescribing pedestrian interventions
summary: Researching candidate only. Official datasets make corridor discovery plausible, but record-level joinability, exposure, mechanism, owner, and field evidence are not yet established.
observed_condition: Taoyuan publishes A1/A2 road-accident records with time, road/intersection and coordinates, along with separate accident-hotspot, sidewalk-management, and real-time roadway datasets that could support candidate-corridor discovery.
unresolved_core: Determine whether the available datasets can identify stable corridors that merit field investigation and whether subsequent evidence can distinguish geometry, exposure, signal timing, visibility, behavior, or another mechanism without making a premature causal claim.
time_scope: Official accident records currently described for ROC 106–114 (2017–2025); other resource freshness varies by source.
disputes_uncertainty: No record-level accident/sidewalk join has yet been verified in this pilot.
Accident counts without an exposure denominator can mis-rank risk.
Road-level sidewalk measurements may not represent intersection-level geometry or continuity.
Public datasets alone do not establish a causal mechanism or justify a specific road intervention.
A competent local problem owner/domain reviewer has not yet accepted this formulation.
diagnosis: No binding mechanism is accepted yet; geometry, signal timing, exposure, visibility, behavior, and data artifacts remain competing explanations.
knowledge_frontier: Verify field definitions, missingness, temporal coverage, and geospatial joinability.
Define a non-causal candidate-corridor ranking before mechanism claims.
Determine whether a defensible exposure proxy is available or must be collected.
Obtain transport/domain review and representative observation for any shortlisted location.
constraints: Do not infer causality from co-location alone.
Do not identify a location as unsafe for public release until the evidence/owner review supports that wording.
Any road, signal, enforcement, or other consequential intervention requires competent authority.
Preserve government dataset licensing and source attribution.
authority_boundary: This candidate authorizes research and public-data analysis only. Any field intervention, road/signal change, or official safety determination requires the competent Taoyuan authority/operator.
implementation_pathway: Produce a non-causal shortlist with uncertainty.
Collect representative observations for selected candidates.
Reframe, verify, or retire the Problem Packet before any intervention proposal.
rights_notes: The referenced government datasets state Government Open Data License Taiwan 1.0 where indicated; linked materials retain their own terms. This draft does not copy raw datasets into the repository.

evidence.source: Taiwan Government Open Data Platform / Taoyuan City Police Department
evidence.summary: Official metadata describes annual A1/A2 accident records by time, area, road/intersection, with longitude/latitude available from ROC 106 onward and current coverage through ROC 114.
disputes: Metadata availability does not establish any candidate corridor or causal mechanism.

evidence.source: Taiwan Government Open Data Platform / Taoyuan City Department of Public Works
evidence.summary: Official metadata describes road-level sidewalk length/width and road dimensions by district/road.
disputes: Road-level fields may not represent intersection geometry, continuity, obstruction, or pedestrian exposure.

evidence.summary: Official hotspot metadata includes year/month, district, accident/place/vehicle categories, case count, deaths, injuries, and case information.
disputes: Hotspot aggregation is a discovery aid, not a causal diagnosis.

evidence.source: Taoyuan Open Data Platform / Transportation Department
evidence.summary: The city publishes minute-level roadway travel time, speed, congestion and data-collection metadata for road sections.
disputes: Roadway speed/congestion may not be an adequate pedestrian exposure measure.

success_criteria.baseline: Metadata-only candidate with no validated join or mechanism.
success_criteria.target: A transport/domain reviewer agrees that the packet identifies a defensible investigation frontier and avoids unsupported causal/intervention claims.
success_criteria.measurement: Independent review of source definitions, shortlist method, uncertainty, and proposed field-observation plan.
success_criteria.falsification: Datasets cannot be joined/interpreted defensibly, no stable investigation frontier emerges, or reviewer determines that the formulation overstates what the evidence can support.
guardrails: No causal claim from co-location alone
